decisions.quote: A replication of the New Haven experiment reproduces both the findings reported in Gerber and Green 2000 and the biases of Imai’s statistical analysis.
decisions.location: Abstract, p. 301 (see also 'Replication Confirms Original Results', pp. 303-304)
decisions.reason: This hybrid paper both reconstructs/corrects the original 1998 New Haven dataset from Gerber and Green (2000) and reports a new large-scale field experiment conducted in November 2002 in Iowa and Michigan (N > 1.9 million) designed to replicate the 1998 New Haven study. Because the paper collects new data in an independent sample to re-test Gerber and Green (2000), the shipped coding of 'replication' is supported by the full text.

decisions.reason: The shipped outcome quote is verified in the abstract (differing only in the typographic apostrophe in 'Imai’s'), and in the section 'Replication Confirms Original Results' (pp. 303-304) the authors conclude that the 2002 Iowa and Michigan replication experiment confirms the original 1998 New Haven findings reported in Gerber and Green (2000) ( additively reinforced by the corrected 1998 data analysis leaving all substantive conclusions unchanged).

decisions.quote: Replication of Professor Imai’s (2005) analysis reveals a series of errors that call into question the magnitude, significance, and robustness of his matching estimates.
decisions.location: Introduction, p. 301 (see also Table 2 and pp. 308-310)
decisions.reason: Omitted target: Under the codebook rules for replication chains and earlier replication/reanalysis attempts, an earlier reanalysis is a target when the current paper directly re-tests its findings. Gerber and Green (2005) directly re-runs Imai (2005)'s propensity score matching code and analysis on the dataset Imai analyzed (Table 2, pp. 308-310), demonstrating computational discrepancies and robustness failures, and also tests Imai's 6.5 percentage point estimate in the 2002 replication experiment.
